sheet-52.description: This additional sheet of the Morristown atlas, dated January 1923 and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows part of the grounds of the New Jersey State Hospital for the Insane (later Greystone Park Psychiatric Hospital) at Morris Plains. The page is turned so that north lies about 48 degrees clockwise from the top. Its only street is Central Avenue, drawn as a straight 100 ft avenue running down the middle of the sheet from a dashed curving drive at the top, which leads towards the main hospital buildings shown on sheet 49, south-eastward to the bottom edge. A 6 inch water pipe runs along the avenue with branches to hydrants. West of the avenue, near the top, stand two brick nurses' homes and a recreation hall labelled State Hospital for the Insane, and near the bottom two frame doctor's homes. East of the avenue is the Psychiatric Clinic, a long brick building with steel frame and concrete floors, with wards at both ends, clinic day rooms, a dining room and a kitchen; another doctor's home stands at the bottom edge on each side of the avenue. Two further buildings are drawn at the top of the sheet without labels. The rest of the sheet is open hospital ground, left blank, with a note referring to the report on sheet 49. A blue water feature is cut by the top edge at the head of the avenue.
notes: Caption title Morristown, N.J.; headed Additional Sheet, January 1923; refers to the report on sheet 49, which is not part of this record.
Central Avenue keeps its name; its straight north-western stretch in OpenStreetMap matches the drawn avenue in direction.
Modern Medical Drive, John J. Murphy Way and Old Dover Road cross the area the sheet covers but are not drawn; they were laid out later or not mapped by Sanborn.

No street junction is drawn: the sheet is placed from one hand-picked point (the north-west end of Central Avenue at the hospital drive) with the printed scale and the direction of modern Central Avenue; position along the avenue is uncertain.
